stem: The irony of this quotation is that it calls attention to —
instruction:
Read this quotation from paragraph 20.

"It's our earth. It's our land. Can't nobody touch a man's own land."

options.label: A
options.text: the love T. J. has for the outdoors while he is on a man-made structure

options.label: B
options.text: the rooftop being abandoned and the men still caring about its welfare

options.label: C
options.text: the fact that T. J. does not have the right to use the rooftop despite creating the garden

options.label: D
options.text: the effort used to create a garden when it can be easily destroyed

visual_elements: "It's our earth. It's our land. Can't nobody touch a man's own land."
